summary:
Belgorod Oblast stands under the national framework that Russia applies across all of its regions, and the UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (June 2025, assessment section updated 11 June 2025) sets out the conditions in force here. Same-sex activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and legal gender transition are banned, trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023, and no discrimination legislation based on sexual orientation or gender identity covers housing, healthcare or employment. The note records no region-specific findings; it states the national conditions that govern this region as it does every other.

Public expression is criminalised in terms that reach gender transition directly. 'Gay propaganda' offences carry fines of up to 400,000 roubles (about £3,600) for individuals or up to 15 days' detention, repeat offences can bring criminal prosecution with up to four years in prison, and the November 2023 Supreme Court 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement makes participation punishable by 2 to 6 years and organising by 6 to 10 years. Between December 2022 and March 2024 at least 139 people were affected by enforcement of anti-LGBT+ laws, and the note assesses trans people, publicly active LGBT+ advocates, and those in the North Caucasus as likely to face treatment amounting to persecution.

Human Rights Watch reported on 30 June 2025 that Russian courts had issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions tied to the International Public LGBT Movement designation, approximately 98 administrative and three criminal. The Supreme Court ruling of November 2023 entered into force in January 2024 and opened the way to arbitrary prosecutions of LGBT people and their supporters. Between January 2024 and June 2025 at least 20 people faced criminal charges under the designation, two were sentenced to prison, and one died by suicide in pretrial detention; 81 people in 98 court cases were found guilty of administrative offences for displaying banned symbols, with fines up to 2,000 roubles and repeat displays punishable under the criminal code by up to four years in prison. On 15 May 2025 investigators charged three publishing-house staff under article 282.2 for selling fiction exploring LGBT themes, an offence carrying up to 12 years.

A foreign-government travel advisory for Russia states that official support for travellers is 'very limited' in parts of the country. None of the sources reviewed records any region-specific finding for Belgorod Oblast; the enforcement climate described above is national and applies here as everywhere else in Russia.
tangentialFactors:
The enforcement pattern documented by Human Rights Watch is national in scope, so the risk profile in Belgorod Oblast mirrors that of Moscow, St Petersburg and other regions rather than differing from them. The designation regime has produced convictions in both administrative and criminal tracks within eighteen months of the ruling taking force, indicating sustained rather than episodic enforcement.

The publishing-house charges of May 2025 show that the extremism provisions reach ordinary commercial activity, not only advocacy or public demonstration, which broadens the categories of conduct that can draw scrutiny.
localsOnly:
Residents of Belgorod Oblast face the same legal exposure as all Russian residents: administrative fines for displaying banned symbols, criminal prosecution for repeat offences, and the severe participation and organisation penalties attached to the extremist designation. Legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care are unavailable, and no anti-discrimination statute covers employment, housing or healthcare on grounds of gender identity or sexual orientation.

The UK Home Office note treats trans people and publicly active LGBT+ advocates as a particular social group likely to face persecution, which sets the standard for UK asylum claims arising from this region.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in the inventory records enforcement actions, raids, arrests or court cases specific to Belgorod Oblast; the region-specific picture is unresolved on the available material, and the national figures cited cannot be apportioned to this oblast.

The exact current exchange value of the 400,000-rouble and 2,000-rouble fines in sterling is not sourced here beyond the note's approximate conversion.
